title: A Hundred Dollars to Fumble

lines.speaker: TITLE
lines.visual: card:Toledo, Ohio|A Hundred Dollars to Fumble

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Toledo, Ohio. The Glass City. Home of the Rockets. And for a couple of seasons in the middle of the two thousands, home of the cheapest fix in college sports.
lines.caption: Toledo, Ohio. The Glass City. Home of the Rockets. And for a couple of seasons in the middle of the two thousands, home of the cheapest fix in college sports.

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Point shaving? That is a big-city racket. Boston College. The mob. Not Toledo. And I am a Bowling Green man, I would love to believe it.
lines.caption: Point shaving? That is a big-city racket. Boston College. The mob. Not Toledo. And I am a Bowling Green man, I would love to believe it.

lines.speaker: CLIP
lines.caption: Toledo at Bowling Green, overtime, November 22, 2005 (Toledo won 44-41). ESPN2 broadcast, used under fair use for commentary.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: Gary, it is an hour up the road from Detroit.
lines.caption: Gary, it is an hour up the road from Detroit.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Two gamblers from the Detroit area. Ghazi Manni and his partner, Mitchell Karam. From about 2004 to 2006 they made friends with Toledo football and basketball players.
lines.caption: Two gamblers from the Detroit area. Ghazi Manni and his partner, Mitchell Karam. From about 2004 to 2006 they made friends with Toledo football and basketball players.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: And they did not need much to do it. Players told the court they took money, meals and groceries.
lines.caption: And they did not need much to do it. Players told the court they took money, meals and groceries.
lines.visual: card:Money, meals and groceries|What players told the court

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Groceries.
lines.caption: Groceries.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: Groceries, Gary. These were college kids without a dime. Somebody buys you dinner and asks how the team looks this week.
lines.caption: Groceries, Gary. These were college kids without a dime. Somebody buys you dinner and asks how the team looks this week.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Then he asks for a little more. And nobody had to lose a game. That is the part people get wrong about point shaving. You win by six instead of ten. The scoreboard says Toledo, and the gambler cashes anyway.
lines.caption: Then he asks for a little more. And nobody had to lose a game. That is the part people get wrong about point shaving. You win by six instead of ten. The scoreboard says Toledo, and the gambler cashes anyway.
lines.visual: card:Point shaving|Win by six instead of ten

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: One running back took more than two thousand dollars in cash and goods. By the government's account, that included one hundred dollars to fumble in the 2005 GMAC Bowl.
lines.caption: One running back took more than two thousand dollars in cash and goods. By the government's account, that included one hundred dollars to fumble in the 2005 GMAC Bowl.
lines.visual: card:$100|To fumble in a bowl game, by the government's account

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: A hundred dollars? In a bowl game? On television?
lines.caption: A hundred dollars? In a bowl game? On television?

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: One hundred dollars. And here is the part I can't get past. Toledo won that game forty-five to thirteen.
lines.caption: One hundred dollars. And here is the part I can't get past. Toledo won that game forty-five to thirteen.

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: They won by thirty-two and a fella still got paid to drop the ball.
lines.caption: They won by thirty-two and a fella still got paid to drop the ball.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: That is how small it is, Gary. One play. Nobody in the stadium would ever know.
lines.caption: That is how small it is, Gary. One play. Nobody in the stadium would ever know.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: The government counted about four hundred thousand dollars in bets on Toledo basketball alone.
lines.caption: The government counted about four hundred thousand dollars in bets on Toledo basketball alone.
lines.visual: card:About $407,500|Bet on Toledo basketball, November 2005 to December 2006

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: So the players got lunch money and the gamblers got rich.
lines.caption: So the players got lunch money and the gamblers got rich.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: And here is who caught it, Gary. A Las Vegas casino. In October 2005, MGM saw strange money on Toledo games and called the Nevada regulators. By that December the FBI was listening to the gambler's phone.
lines.caption: And here is who caught it, Gary. A Las Vegas casino. In October 2005, MGM saw strange money on Toledo games and called the Nevada regulators. By that December the FBI was listening to the gambler's phone.
lines.visual: card:October 2005|MGM reports unusual betting on Toledo games

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: The casino called the cops.
lines.caption: The casino called the cops.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: That is the usual arrangement. Seven former Rockets pleaded guilty. The judge gave them probation. He said what they did was out of character, and it was ten years gone.
lines.caption: That is the usual arrangement. Seven former Rockets pleaded guilty. The judge gave them probation. He said what they did was out of character, and it was ten years gone.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: One of them stood outside the courthouse and said this. I had issues, gambling issues. I was depressed at the time. I made poor decisions.
lines.caption: One of them stood outside the courthouse and said this. I had issues, gambling issues. I was depressed at the time. I made poor decisions.
lines.visual: card:“I had issues, gambling issues. I was depressed at the time. I made poor decisions.”|A former Toledo player, March 2015

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Well. That is a kid talking. That is not a gangster.
lines.caption: Well. That is a kid talking. That is not a gangster.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And one more thing belongs in the record. In 2006 a player was asked to help fix a game against Iowa State. He said no.
lines.caption: And one more thing belongs in the record. In 2006 a player was asked to help fix a game against Iowa State. He said no.
lines.visual: card:He said no.|Asked to help fix the 2006 Iowa State game

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: Nobody wrote a headline about him.
lines.caption: Nobody wrote a headline about him.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: The gambler Manni got seventy months in federal prison, on a plea that also covered fixed horse races and food stamp fraud.
lines.caption: The gambler Manni got seventy months in federal prison, on a plea that also covered fixed horse races and food stamp fraud.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: Now think about when this happened. Sports betting was against the law almost everywhere. You had to know a guy.
lines.caption: Now think about when this happened. Sports betting was against the law almost everywhere. You had to know a guy.

lines.speaker: CLIP
lines.caption: Arena video by Matthew Hagan, Miami. Neon effect generated with AI.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Today the guy is an app. DraftKings and FanDuel are on the broadcast, on the scoreboard, and on the phone in your pocket. You can bet a Tuesday night MAC game, right down to one player's rebounds.
lines.caption: Today the guy is an app. DraftKings and FanDuel are on the broadcast, on the scoreboard, and on the phone in your pocket. You can bet a Tuesday night MAC game, right down to one player's rebounds.

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Well, at least it is all legal and out in the open now. That ought to keep it clean.
lines.caption: Well, at least it is all legal and out in the open now. That ought to keep it clean.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: Does it, Gary?
lines.caption: Does it, Gary?

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Right now the Cleveland Guardians' closer is on trial in Brooklyn, charged with selling his pitches for a few thousand dollars. Terry Rozier, an NBA guard, goes to trial in February. Both men say they are not guilty. And notice whose names you know. The player. It is always the player.
lines.caption: Right now the Cleveland Guardians' closer is on trial in Brooklyn, charged with selling his pitches for a few thousand dollars. Terry Rozier, an NBA guard, goes to trial in February. Both men say they are not guilty. And notice whose names you know. The player. It is always the player.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: That closer had a twenty million dollar contract. Prosecutors say he also owed the IRS half a million dollars.
lines.caption: That closer had a twenty million dollar contract. Prosecutors say he also owed the IRS half a million dollars.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Now look up the food chain. Last year Massachusetts regulators found that the legal sportsbooks cut down the bets of customers who win too often. The sharp ones. The ones who do the homework. And they hand the VIP status and the rewards mostly to the people who lose.
lines.caption: Now look up the food chain. Last year Massachusetts regulators found that the legal sportsbooks cut down the bets of customers who win too often. The sharp ones. The ones who do the homework. And they hand the VIP status and the rewards mostly to the people who lose.
lines.visual: card:Winners limited. Losers made VIPs.|Massachusetts Gaming Commission, September 2025

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Hold on. They throw out the winners and give the losers a host?
lines.caption: Hold on. They throw out the winners and give the losers a host?

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: One man lost one point eight million dollars, Gary. His FanDuel VIP manager sent him a personal video from a big league star.
lines.caption: One man lost one point eight million dollars, Gary. His FanDuel VIP manager sent him a personal video from a big league star.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And how did all of this get legal? The New York Times found the industry's lobbyists lavished state lawmakers with gifts, parties and millions of dollars in donations.
lines.caption: And how did all of this get legal? The New York Times found the industry's lobbyists lavished state lawmakers with gifts, parties and millions of dollars in donations.
lines.visual: card:“Gifts, parties and millions of dollars in donations”|The New York Times, November 2022

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: So a college kid takes a hundred dollars, and it is a federal case. A company limits the winners, rewards the losers, and wines and dines the statehouse, and it is a business model. Ask yourself again. Who is the real criminal?
lines.caption: So a college kid takes a hundred dollars, and it is a federal case. A company limits the winners, rewards the losers, and wines and dines the statehouse, and it is a business model. Ask yourself again. Who is the real criminal?
lines.visual: card:Who is the real criminal?|DraftKings and FanDuel say they invest in responsible gaming

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: A hundred dollars to fumble. I take it back about Toledo.
lines.caption: A hundred dollars to fumble. I take it back about Toledo.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: We run betting lines on this site. So we ought to be the first ones to say it out loud.
lines.caption: We run betting lines on this site. So we ought to be the first ones to say it out loud.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Toledo, Ohio. Keep it real.
lines.caption: Toledo, Ohio. Keep it real.
